question: Which of the following is NOT a hydroelectric power plant?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sambhar Lake Hydel Project**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sambhar Lake** is India’s largest inland saltwater lake located in Rajasthan and is primarily used for salt production, not for hydroelectric power generation.
 
• Hydroelectric power plants utilize flowing water to generate electricity, typically requiring dams or significant water flow, which Sambhar Lake lacks.
 
• Other listed projects like **Bhakra Nangal**, **Damodar Valley**, and **Kopili Hydel Project** are well-known hydroelectric power plants in India.
 
• Sambhar Lake is significant for its ecological and economic value but does not contribute to India’s hydroelectric power infrastructure.
 
• Hydroelectric power plants are typically located in regions with ample freshwater resources and elevation changes, which Sambhar Lake does not possess.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydroelectric Power:**

 
 
• Hydroelectric power is the generation of electricity using water flow through turbines.
 
• It is a renewable energy source that contributes significantly to India’s energy mix.
 
• India has several major hydropower projects including Bhakra Nangal, Tehri Dam, and Sardar Sarovar Dam.
 
 
 
• **Sambhar Lake:**
 
 
• Located in Rajasthan, Sambhar Lake spans over 190 square kilometers.
 
• It is a Ramsar site, recognized for its ecological importance and migratory bird habitats.
 
• The lake is a major contributor to India’s salt production but lacks infrastructure for electricity generation.
 
 
 
• **Bhakra Nangal Hydel Project:**
 
 
• Situated on the Sutlej River, this project is one of India’s largest hydropower facilities.
 
• It serves multiple purposes, including electricity generation, irrigation, and flood control.
 
 
 
• **Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC):**
 
 
• Established in 1948, DVC operates several hydropower and thermal power plants.
 
• Its hydropower plants are located in Jharkhand and West Bengal.
